title: menuz: a macOS menu bar app whose menu is a YAML file of commands to run
objective:
A new utility, `menuz`, that puts a menu of hv's own commands in the macOS menu bar. The menu is entirely a YAML file in a menuz config directory: the file says what the menu holds, each item runs something (a script, a `utilz` verb, any shell line), an item that needs parameters acquires them from the user before it runs, and whatever a run prints goes to one known `menuz.log` that can be tailed. The app reads its whole menu from the config files, notices when they change and updates the menu, and realises the variables in the menu each time the menu is displayed. The first thing on the menu is `arngz`: apply a desk from the menu bar.

Three working menu bar apps already exist in sibling projects (Intent.app, Conflab.app, Gtools.app), all one shape: an xcodegen project, an `AppDelegate` with an `NSStatusItem`, the login shell's `PATH` handed to every child, `SMAppService` for launch at login, Apple Development signing, build products off the tree, and an `install` verb that builds Release, replaces the bundle under `~/Applications` and launches it with launchd's environment. menuz is that shape cut to a menu read from a file, and it invents nothing the shell or macOS already does: variable interpolation is the login shell's own expansion, parameters are acquired through macOS's standard dialogs, the log is a file `tail -f` reads.

v1 is: the app (the menu from the file, watched, realised at open; parameters; the runner; the log and the notice), and the `utilz menuz` shim with `init`, `edit`, `log`, `validate`, `render`, `build`, `test`, `install`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `status`, `stamps` and `doctor`.
context:
Asked by hv on 16 Oct 2026, directly to vc, just before a compact: "a very simple macOS (Swift) menu bar app that is entirely customisable from a yaml file that points to a .menuz config directory (in the appropriate location for that kind of dir) ... The main use case for menuz is for me to be able to run a list of common utilities easily by just selecting them from the menubar. The obvious one that I want to try is arngz." hv asked for the write-up first and a rubber-duck session to refine it before any code, and added two standing instructions on the bounce: the three sibling menu bar apps (`../Intent`, `../Conflab`, `../Gtools`) are the pattern, "we DO NOT need to reinvent the wheel here"; and nothing is rebuilt that macOS or the standard unix utilities already do, interpolation included.

The thread is created and started ahead of the rubber-duck: design.md carries the shape, the questions hv left open with vc's recommendation on each, and the work packages. The design's open questions are settled with hv before WP-02 starts; WP-01 is that settlement. Doc before code holds: no source under opt/menuz until the design stands.

wps.title: Design settled with hv
wps.body:
## Decisions

hv ruled on 16 Oct 2026 in vc's session, the rubber-duck of WP-01. In hv's words where hv gave them.

| D   | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D1  | As recommended: the config directory is `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/menuz/`, `MENUZ_HOME` overriding.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| D2  | As recommended: Yams parses the yaml in the app, Codable models, one parser.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D3  | As recommended: interpolation is the login shell's own expansion of labels and `each` lines, one `zsh -ilc` per menu open, asynchronous, the last values shown first, capped. No menuz syntax.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| D4  | hv: "One form with all params, typed (where possible)." One window per run holding every param, each field typed from the param's `type` (text, secret, choice, file, folder; `text` when none is given). Not the standard dialogs.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D5  | As recommended: `menuz.log` under XDG state, `utilz menuz log` tails it, a notification on a non-zero exit, `notify:` per item.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D6  | hv, first to vc: "It's built here locally for dev in native/macos like the other menbar apps, and the installed into opt. There should be a 'use dev\|opt' option like the way devbin has that feature." Then, in cc's session, hv asked where Intent.app, Conflab.app and Gtools.app live, "we should be consistent", and picked the siblings' target (confirmed to vc: "See the utilz-cc correction on install location"). So: the source and the xcodegen project at `native/macos/Menuz/`; the dev build under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos/Build/Products/<Config>/`, as Intent's and Gtools' do; the installed copy at `~/Applications/Menuz.app`, Gtools' and Conflab's target (Intent's signed release goes to /Applications); a `use dev\|installed` switch, after devbin's own, says which the shim's launch and status use. |
| D7  | hv: "Same as Intent. This is opensource just like Intent and it needs to be signed properly." Developer ID, notarised, shipped as a release asset the keg installs; not the Apple Development model.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| D8  | As recommended: the menu bar glyph is an SF Symbol named in the yaml, `terminal` by default; no asset pipeline. (hv's "8: Left running" is read as Q9, since "left running" is Q9's alternative; hv is told so.)                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| D9  | hv: "Left running, surely?" Runs in flight at Quit are left running, detached from the app (their own session, stdin from /dev/null, stdout and stderr on the log file directly rather than through the app), so the app's exit closes nothing they write to. The log records the quit and names the runs still going.                                                                                                             |
| D10 | hv: "Yep": `each` is in v1.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| D11 | hv: "Yep, agree": `Menuz.app`, `com.matthewsinclair.utilz.menuz`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

wps.title: The shim, the config directory and the catalogue verbs
wps.objective:
The `utilz menuz` shim: a bash script in the Utilz format, the menuz config directory, and the verbs that need no Xcode. It follows D1 to D11 as recorded in WP-01, D6 as hv corrected it on 16 Oct 2026. Where design.md's shim and build-layout sections disagree with those rulings, the rulings win, and design.md is rewritten at the 0605 sync.

**Files.**

- `opt/menuz/menuz` is the shim. It is bash 3.2-clean under `set -euo pipefail` and shellcheck-clean.
- `opt/menuz/menuz.yaml` declares the utility, with `version_file: VERSION` and `dependencies: []`. xcodegen and xcodebuild are build-time needs, so the shim refuses by name without them, as it does for cargo.
- `opt/menuz/VERSION` is the one home of the version.
- `opt/menuz/lib/example.yaml` is the design's example menu, which `init` writes. Its one param is typed (`type: string`), per D4.
- `bin/menuz` is a symlink to `utilz`, and CI's explicit Linux utility loop gains `menuz`.

**Paths, each in one function.**

| What               | Path                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Config directory   | `${MENUZ_HOME:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/menuz}`                                                                    |
| The menu           | `<config>/menuz.yaml`                                                                                                      |
| Log                | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/menuz.log`                                                                    |
| Dev build          | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos/Build/Products/Debug/Menuz.app`                                   |
| Installed copy     | `$HOME/Applications/Menuz.app`                                                                                             |
| The `use` record   | `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/use`, holding `dev` or `installed`, written by WP-05's `use` verb             |

The build `use` selects is the one the record names. With no record, it is the installed copy when there is one, else the dev build. The app binary is `<bundle>/Contents/MacOS/Menuz` of that build.

**Verbs.** Exit codes follow arngz: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 refused before anything changed. `menuz` with no verb prints usage and exits 2.

| Verb                        | Does                                                                                                                                                                     | Exit                                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init [--force]`            | Creates the config directory with the example `menuz.yaml` and an empty `bin/`. A second run changes nothing                                                             | 0; 2 when `menuz.yaml` exists without `--force`, naming it |
| `edit [--editor]`           | `open -t menuz.yaml`; with `--editor`, `$VISUAL`, else `$EDITOR`                                                                                                         | 0; 2 with no `menuz.yaml`, or `--editor` with neither set  |
| `log [-n N]`                | Prints the log's path, then `tail -f`; with `-n N`, the last N lines and no follow                                                                                       | 0; 2 with no log yet                                      |
| `validate [file]`           | The selected app binary's `--validate` on the file or `menuz.yaml`, its output and exit passed through                                                                  | the app's; 2 with no app, naming both build paths         |
| `render [file]`             | The same with `--render`                                                                                                                                                 | the same                                                  |
| `status`                    | One line each for installed (path, version, build, commit), use (dev or installed, and whether by the record or by default), running, login item and source           | 0; 1 when not installed                                   |

**Status details.**

- **Running** is `pgrep -x Menuz`, the pids or `no`.
- **Login item** is the selected app's answer to a new arm, `--login-item`, which prints the `SMAppService.mainApp` status. WP-03 adds the arm to the app's command-line arms. With no app, the line says so.
- **Source** compares the installed bundle's `MenuzSourceTree` (Info.plist) with the stamp of the tree, as Gtools does. The stamp is a SHA-1 of `git ls-tree -r HEAD native/macos/Menuz` without `MenuzTests/`. A dirty tree folds in each changed path and a digest of its content, and the stamp ends `-dirty`. With no `native/macos/Menuz`, the source is unknown and said so. WP-05's `stamps` and `build` use the same function.

`status` reads Info.plist with `/usr/libexec/PlistBuddy` and needs no Xcode.

**utilz doctor** checks xcodegen and xcodebuild only when `native/macos/Menuz` is present, beside the crate rule in common.sh, advisory as cargo is.

**Tests.** `opt/menuz/test/menuz.bats`, red first, with these fixtures:

- `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME` and `MENUZ_HOME` all point under `BATS_TEST_TMPDIR`.
- A fake `Menuz.app` sits at the installed or dev path: an executable that records its arguments and prints a scripted answer, with an Info.plist.
- `open`, `pgrep` and `tail` are fakes on PATH where a verb would otherwise reach the machine.

wps.title: The app: the menu from the file, watched, realised at open
wps.objective:
The app, `Menuz.app`: its menu read from the file, validated, watched, and realised at each open, plus the command-line arms. Running items (the form, the runner, the run log, the notice) is WP-04; build, install, `use` and signing are WP-05. This note settles what design.md leaves open for WP-03. design.md's sections are the contract, with D1 to D11 as recorded in WP-01.

**Layout: a pure package and an app over it.** `swift test` must run the pure parts without an Xcode build, so they live in a local Swift package that the app links.

| Path                             | What                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `native/macos/Menuz/project.yml` | xcodegen, Gtools' cut: Swift 6, macOS 14, `LSUIElement`, Automatic signing with team 76BQL8L47U for Debug and Release, hardened runtime, the stamps as build settings                     |
| `native/macos/Menuz/MenuzKit/`   | A Swift package: the `MenuzKit` library (depends on Yams 6) and its `MenuzKitTests` test target. Everything pure lives here, with no AppKit                                               |
| `native/macos/Menuz/Menuz/`      | The app: `MenuzApp.swift` (the delegate and the arms), `Services/` (`LoginShell`, `Watcher`, `Realiser`, `MenuBuilder`, `AppLog`), `Info.plist`, entitlements                             |
| `native/macos/Menuz/MenuzTests/` | A unit-test bundle hosted by the app: the test-host guard, and anything that needs AppKit. The scheme runs it and `MenuzKitTests`, so `xcodebuild test` and `utilz menuz test` cover both |

Yams is the one package, a dependency of MenuzKit (D2). The bundle id is `com.matthewsinclair.utilz.menuz` (D11). Info.plist substitutes `MENUZ_VERSION`, `MENUZ_BUILD`, `MENUZ_COMMIT` and `MENUZ_SOURCE_TREE` into `CFBundleShortVersionString`, `CFBundleVersion`, `MenuzCommit` and `MenuzSourceTree`, the keys WP-02's `status` reads. A build from Xcode gets `dev`.

**MenuzKit, the pure parts.**

- **One parse.** `MenuLoader.load(text:file:context:)` composes the YAML into a Yams `Node` once. The validator walks that node and builds the models (`MenuFile`, `Entry`, `Param`) in the same walk, so a file it passes is never parsed twice. Amended 16 Oct at the build: a Codable decode was the first plan and is not used. It cannot name the entry path a refusal needs, and YAML's core schema would type `run: true` as a Bool and `cwd: ~` as null where the file means the text; the walk reads every value as the scalar's text as written.
- **Refusals beyond the seven rules**, each so that nothing in a file is silently dropped: a key given twice; a key that is not a single word; a value that must be one string and is a list or a mapping; `separator` other than `true`; a submenu's `items` empty; `choices` empty, or given with a type other than `choice`; `required` other than `true` or `false`; an entry or a param that is not a mapping. An `each` without a `label`, a `submenu` without `items` and `items` without a `submenu` are refused by the key that is wrong.
- **The validator** is a function of the node and two facts it is given: the names the login shell exports (rule 4) and a predicate for whether an SF Symbol exists (rule 6). It returns every refusal, not the first. A refusal carries the file, the entry path (`menu[4].items[1]`), the key, the value and why, and prints as one line: `<file>: <path>.<key> = '<value>': <why>`. A param with no `type` is `text`.
- **The menu spec** is the validated file as a tree of nodes (item, caption, header, separator, submenu, each), plus the fixed tail. The app builds an `NSMenu` from it. `--render` prints the same spec as indented text, one entry per line, with the realised labels.
- **The realiser's pure half.**
  - A string is dynamic when it holds `$` or a backtick. A literal is never sent to the shell.
  - Every dynamic label and every `each` line of a menu is realised in one script, run by one `zsh -ilc`.
  - Each label is expanded as the body of a double-quoted string (`eval` of `"<label>"`), each in its own subshell, so one that fails costs only itself.
  - Each `each` line is run, and for every line it prints, `MENUZ_ITEM` is set and that entry's label is expanded.
  - Each result comes back framed as `<id> US <status> US <value> RS`.
  - The script builder and the parser of its output are pure and tested. A test also runs the script through `/bin/zsh -c` (not `-il`, so it is hermetic).
- **The paths.** `MENUZ_HOME`, the config file and the log are found from an environment dictionary, the way the shim finds them. The app passes the login shell's capture, because launchd gives a GUI app none of the user's variables.
- **The log line**: an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, then the text. WP-03 writes refusals and realise overruns. WP-04 adds the run lines.

**The app.**

- **The delegate** is Gtools' shape: `@main @MainActor final class AppDelegate`, `isTestHost` returning before any launch path, an Edit menu for an `LSUIElement` app, and the status item's glyph from the file's `icon` (an SF Symbol, `terminal` by default), never zero width. The app registers itself with `SMAppService.mainApp` on its first run, logs a failure, and never registers silently.
- **The login shell** is captured once per launch by `/bin/zsh -ilc`: `PATH` plus `MENUZ_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, and the exported names rule 4 needs. Reload captures it again.
- **The watcher** is Conflab's: `DispatchSource` file-system sources on `O_EVTONLY` descriptors for the directory and the file (`.write`, `.delete`, `.rename`). It coalesces events over 250 ms, reopens the file's descriptor after a rename or a delete, and retries a missing directory every 5 s. GCD here is the API macOS gives for vnode events; the coalescing and the reload are a `Task` on the main actor.
- **A file that fails** keeps the last good menu and adds the refusal as a disabled first item in red. The refusal also goes to `menuz.log` and OSLog. A file that fails at launch shows the refusal and the tail alone.
- **The realiser's impure half** runs in `menuWillOpen`, off the main actor. The menu shows the last values at once (the file's text the first time), and titles change in place when the shell answers; `each` items are replaced in place. Past `realise` seconds the shell is stopped, every label not yet answered keeps its last value, and the overrun is logged.
- **The tail**: a separator, **Edit Menu…** (`open -t` on the file), **Open Log** (`open` on the log, or a disabled line saying none exists yet), **Reload**, **Quit menuz** (Cmd-Q). Items with `run` are listed in WP-03 and do nothing until WP-04's runner exists. Choosing one logs that running is not built yet. No item is ever silently dead.

**The arms**, read in `main()` before `NSApplication` starts. They touch no menu bar and exit:

| Arm                 | Prints                                                                                         | Exit                      |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `--validate [file]` | `ok`, or every refusal, one per line                                                           | 0, or 2                   |
| `--render [file]`   | The menu as indented text, labels realised through the login shell, the tail included          | 0, or 2 with the refusals |
| `--version`         | `<version> (build <build>, <commit>)` from Info.plist                                          | 0                         |
| `--login-item`      | `SMAppService.mainApp.status`: `enabled`, `requires approval`, `not registered` or `not found` | 0                         |

`[file]` defaults to the config file found from the login shell's environment. An unknown arm is refused, exit 2.

**Tests.** MenuzKitTests use Swift Testing, written red first, and are run by `swift test` in `MenuzKit/`. They cover:

- decoding;
- every validation rule, each red on its own fixture and naming file, path, key and value;
- the example passing;
- a param with no type read as text;
- the spec and its render;
- the dynamic test;
- the script builder and output parser, and the script run through zsh;
- `each` expansion;
- path resolution;
- the log line.

MenuzTests holds the test-host guard. The watcher's latency is AC-03.3's hand run, vc's. critic-swift reviews.

wps.title: Running items: params, the runner, the log and the notice
Build, install, launch and the close
wps.objective:
Build, install, launch and the close: the shim's remaining verbs (`build`, `test`, `install`, `use`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `stamps`, `doctor`), the install a keg makes from the signed release asset, the signing and publishing of that asset, and CI. WP-02's verbs (`init`, `edit`, `log`, `validate`, `render`, `status`) stand. This note settles what design.md leaves open for WP-05. design.md's shim table, "Build layout", "CI" and the keg paragraph are the contract, with D6, D7 and D12.

**D12: D7's "same as Intent" is local signing, not CI.** Intent's workflows read no secrets and run no codesign or notarytool. Intent signs and notarises on the maintainer's machine, through its project-local `bin/devbin macos`, with the Apple credentials in the login keychain ("no key material in this repository, in CI config, or in any file this writes"). It publishes the stapled bundle as the release asset `Intent.app.zip`. hv confirmed this reading in cc's session on 16 Oct ("same as intent", "Correct."), and vc recorded it as D12, with design.md's CI paragraph and AC-05.3 reworded to match. So:

- CI builds unsigned and tests, on a tag or a dispatch, and reads no secrets.
- Signing, notarising and attaching the asset are a maintainer's step, on hv's machine.

**Layout.**

| Where                         | What                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `opt/menuz/menuz`             | The verbs below, bash 3.2 under `set -euo pipefail`, shellcheck-clean. Exit codes as arngz: 0 done, 1 failed after changing something (naming the step), 2 refused before anything changed  |
| `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos`       | Project-local, Utilz's own (not the vendored core): `doctor`, `store-creds`, `app-sign`, `app-notarize`, `app-verify`, `publish`, ported from Intent's app half, beside WP-06's `app-icons` |
| `.github/workflows/tests.yml` | The `menuz-app` job                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `opt/menuz/test/menuz.bats`   | The verbs' tests, with fakes on PATH                                                                                                                                                        |
| `opt/menuz/test/macos.bats`   | `bin/devbin macos`'s refusals and sequence, with fakes on PATH                                                                                                                              |

**Source clone or install.** As prez's shim does (ST0014 D5): a tree with `manifest.sha256` at the shim's own tree root is an install, a brew keg or a `utilz install` publish. Neither carries `native/macos/Menuz`, which the published set leaves out. In an install, `build` and `test` refuse by name, exit 2, naming the source clone (`git clone https://github.com/matthewsinclair/utilz`), and `install` takes the release asset (below). In a source clone, `install` builds.

**The first-use fixes are WP-06's (D13), landed ahead of this WP's remainder on hv's "Hold off"; the `--unregister` arm is this WP's.**

**The verbs.**

- **`build [--release] [--unsigned]`**
  - Refuses, exit 2, with no Xcode (`xcodebuild -version` fails), with no `xcodegen`, or with no source tree.
  - Runs `xcodegen generate` only when the project is stale: when `project.yml`, or the set of file paths under `Menuz/`, `MenuzTests/` and `MenuzKit/` (paths, not contents, since a changed source is Xcode's business and a new or removed one is xcodegen's), hashes differently from the hash kept at `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/build/xcodegen.hash`, or when `Menuz.xcodeproj` is absent.
  - Then runs `xcodebuild` Debug, or Release with `--release`. The products and every intermediate go under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/build/macos`, through `-derivedDataPath`, `SYMROOT`, `OBJROOT` and `SHARED_PRECOMPS_DIR` (measured in WP-03: this machine's Xcode location preference otherwise writes into the tree).
  - `--unsigned` adds `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, for a machine with no identity (CI).
  - The stamps are passed as build settings (see `stamps`). A failed `xcodebuild` is exit 1, with its last 40 lines.
- **`test [--unsigned]`**: `xcodebuild test` of the scheme, so MenuzKitTests and MenuzTests both, with the same paths and settings. Exit 1 on a red test, 2 without Xcode or the source.
- **`stamps`** prints what the next build would stamp, one `NAME=value` per line:
  - `MENUZ_VERSION` from `opt/menuz/VERSION`;
  - `MENUZ_BUILD`, the commit count (`git rev-list --count HEAD`);
  - `MENUZ_COMMIT`, the short commit;
  - `MENUZ_SOURCE_TREE`, the tree hash of `native/macos/Menuz`, with `-dirty` when it has uncommitted changes. This is WP-02's `source_stamp`, the one function `status` compares against.

  In an install it prints what the installed bundle carries, and says so.

- **`install`**
  - In a source clone, in order: build Release; quit every running copy by bundle id; replace `~/Applications/Menuz.app`; unclaim the build products; register the installed bundle; launch it.
    - Quitting is JXA's `Application('com.matthewsinclair.utilz.menuz').quit()`, then a wait of up to 5 s for every pid of the bundle id to go.
    - The replacement is a `ditto` to a sibling, then a rename over the old one, so a failure leaves the old copy whole.
    - Unclaiming is `lsregister -u` on the build product, so Launch Services never opens the dev copy for the bundle id.
    - Registering is `lsregister -f` on the installed bundle.
    - The launch is `env -i HOME="$HOME" open -a ~/Applications/Menuz.app`, so the app captures its own login shell rather than inheriting the shim's environment.
    - A step that fails after something changed is exit 1, naming the step. A refusal before any change (no Xcode, no source) is exit 2.
  - In an install: the release asset (below), then the same quit, replace, register and launch.
- **`use [dev|installed]`**: records the choice in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/menuz/use`; with no argument it prints the choice, and why (`installed (default)` when there is no record, D6). `start`, `restart`, `status`, `validate` and `render` act on the chosen build, as WP-02's `selected_build` already does for the last three. Any other word is exit 2.
- **`uninstall`**: quits every copy; asks the installed copy to unregister its login item, through a new arm `--unregister` (`SMAppService.mainApp.unregister()`, printing the result); unregisters the bundle (`lsregister -u`); and removes `~/Applications/Menuz.app`. An unregistration that fails is reported and the removal goes on. Exit 0 when there was nothing installed, saying so.
- **`start`, `stop`, `restart`**:
  - `start` opens the chosen build with an empty environment; it is exit 2 when that build is not there, naming it.
  - `stop` quits every copy by bundle id.
  - `restart` is `stop`, then `start`.
- **`doctor`** prints one line per precondition with its state, exit 1 when any fails:
  - Xcode selected (`xcode-select -p`, `xcodebuild -version`);
  - xcodegen;
  - a Developer ID or Apple Development identity (`security find-identity -v -p codesigning`, counted, never printed whole);
  - `MENUZ_HOME` and its `menuz.yaml`;
  - the yaml valid through the chosen app's `--validate`;
  - the app installed;
  - the app running;
  - the login item.

  In an install it skips the build lines and says why.

- **`status`** gains nothing: WP-02's lines already cover the design's row.

**The release asset.**

- **The name.** `Menuz.app.zip`, as Intent names `Intent.app.zip`. It is a `ditto -c -k --keepParent` of the stapled bundle, with no version in the name: the release's tag carries it.
- **Signing and publishing**, on hv's machine, after `bin/devbin release` has made the release object:
  1. `bin/devbin macos app-sign`: `utilz menuz build --release`, the one build path; a copy staged out of the products; the bundle signed inside-out with the Developer ID identity and the hardened runtime; then the identifier, the team and the runtime flag read back off it.
  2. `bin/devbin macos app-notarize`: `notarytool submit --wait`, the ticket stapled, then a quarantined copy checked by `spctl -a -t exec` for `source=Notarized Developer ID`.
  3. `bin/devbin macos publish`: the zip made and proven again by unzipping it and checking the bundle inside. It is refused if the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString` is not `opt/menuz/VERSION`, if the release object for `VERSION`'s tag does not exist, or if it already holds a `Menuz.app.zip`. Then `gh release upload <tag> Menuz.app.zip`.
- **Credentials.** They live in the login keychain under `utilz.apple.APPLE_ID`, `utilz.apple.APPLE_APP_PASSWORD` and `utilz.apple.APPLE_TEAM_ID`, stored once by `bin/devbin macos store-creds`. That command is interactive and hv's to run. `doctor` reports each as PRESENT or MISSING, never a value. The identity is derived from the team id, as Intent's is.

# ST0027: menuz design

**Status: a write-up for the rubber-duck session with hv. Every "recommended" below is vc's recommendation and not a ruling; the session turns each into a numbered decision (D-n) or a descoping, and WP-01 is done when none is left.**

## The ask

hv, 16 Oct 2026, verbatim essentials: a very simple macOS (Swift) menu bar app, entirely customisable from a yaml file that points to a `.menuz` config directory in the appropriate location for that kind of directory. The yaml defines what goes into the menu; each item does something, eg runs a script. If the script takes params, the menu bar pops up a window and acquires them before running the script and passing them in. If there is output, it is given back to the user after the script runs; hv's simplest option is a known `menuz.log` in an obvious location so it can be tailed. The app reads its entire menu from the config files and is aware of changes so the menu updates. The menu supports variable interpolation, realised each time the menu is displayed. The main use case: hv runs a list of common utilities by selecting them from the menu bar, and the first is `arngz`.

Two instructions from hv on the bounce govern the whole design:

1. Three working menu bar apps exist in `../Intent`, `../Conflab` and `../Gtools`. "We DO NOT need to reinvent the wheel here. We already know how to do this."
2. "Don't reinvent or rebuild something (eg interpolation of the menu bar commands, etc) if there's an accepted pre-existing way to do that. Always default to reusing existing infra on macOS or in the standard unix utils."

## The shape

Two halves, as arngz: a bash shim in the Utilz format (`opt/menuz/menuz`, dispatched by `bin/menuz -> utilz`) and the app (`native/macos/Menuz/`, the siblings' path; `~/Applications/Menuz.app` once installed, D6). The shim builds, installs and drives the app and manages the config directory; the app shows the menu and runs the items. Nothing is computed twice: the yaml is parsed in one place (the app), and the shim's `validate` and `render` ask the app's command-line arms rather than parsing anything themselves.

```
~/.config/menuz/menuz.yaml  --read, watched-->  Menuz.app  --zsh -ilc-->  the item's command
          ^                                        |                         |
          | utilz menuz init|edit|validate|render   | menuWillOpen: realise   | stdout+stderr
          |                                        v                         v
      utilz menuz  <--build|install|use|start|stop-- xcodebuild           ~/.local/state/menuz/menuz.log  <-- utilz menuz log (tail -f)
```

## The config directory

Recommended: `${MENUZ_HOME:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/menuz}` (Q1). It holds:

| Path         | What                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `menuz.yaml` | The menu. The one file the app reads                                                                                                       |
| `bin/`       | Scripts of hv's own. First on `PATH` for every run and every realised label, so `run: backup-notes` finds `bin/backup-notes` with no path  |

`utilz menuz init` creates the directory with the example `menuz.yaml` below and an empty `bin/`, and refuses to overwrite an existing `menuz.yaml` without `--force`. The log is not here: it is state, not configuration, and a config directory is the kind of thing hv keeps in a dotfiles repository.

## The menu file

One document, `menu:` a list of entries, read top to bottom into the menu in order. Four kinds of entry and four keys at the top:

```yaml
# ~/.config/menuz/menuz.yaml
# icon: terminal      # an SF Symbol name for the menu bar glyph; menuz's own mark when absent (D13)
cwd: ~                # where runs start unless an item says otherwise; $HOME when absent
notify: failure       # never | failure | always; what a run's end posts as a notification
realise: 5            # seconds a menu open waits for its labels at most; 5 when absent

menu:
  - header: Desks
  - each: ls "${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/arngz/desks" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\.yaml$//'
    label: "$MENUZ_ITEM"
    run: arngz apply "$MENUZ_ITEM"
  - label: Discover this arrangement
    params:
      - name: desk
        prompt: Save the arrangement on screen now as
        default: today
    run: arngz discover --save "$desk" --force
  - label: Hammerspoon doctor
    run: arngz doctor
    notify: always
  - separator: true
  - submenu: Machine
    items:
      - label: "Up $(uptime | sed 's/.*up //; s/,.*//')"
      - label: Sleep the display
        run: pmset displaysleepnow
      - label: Empty the Trash
        run: osascript -e 'tell application "Finder" to empty trash'
        cwd: ~/.Trash
```

| Entry key   | Meaning                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `label`     | An item. With `run`, choosing it runs the command; without, it is a caption (disabled)                                                                             |
| `run`       | The shell line the login shell executes. Never parsed by menuz                                                                                                     |
| `params`    | A list of parameters acquired before the run (below)                                                                                                               |
| `cwd`       | The run's working directory, this item's over the file's                                                                                                           |
| `notify`    | This item's over the file's                                                                                                                                        |
| `each`      | A shell line whose stdout lines become one item each, realised at every menu open; `$MENUZ_ITEM` is the line, in `label`, `run` and `cwd`                          |
| `header`    | A section header (`NSMenuItem.sectionHeader`, macOS 14)                                                                                                            |
| `separator` | A separator                                                                                                                                                        |
| `submenu`   | A submenu with `items`, the same entries, nested as deep as wanted                                                                                                  |

Below the file's entries the app always adds its own tail: a separator, **Edit Menu…** (opens `menuz.yaml` with `open -t`, so the user's default text editor), **Open Log** (`open` on `menuz.log`), **Reload**, and **Quit menuz** (Cmd-Q). Reload exists for the one case the watcher misses; it is not how changes normally arrive.

### Validation

The validator refuses, naming the file, the entry (by its path, eg `menu[4].items[1]`), the key and the value:

1. An unknown key anywhere.
2. An entry that is none of the four kinds, or more than one (`label` with `header`, `each` with `submenu`).
3. `run` without `label` or `each`; `params` without `run`.
4. A param whose `name` is not `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, or a name the login shell already exports (measured at validation, so `path` is refused on a machine whose shell exports `path`), or two params with one name.
5. A param `type` outside `text`, `secret`, `choice`, `file`, `folder`; `choice` without `choices`.
6. `notify` outside `never`, `failure`, `always`; `realise` not a positive number; `icon` not an SF Symbol this macOS has (`NSImage(systemSymbolName:)` returns nil).
7. An empty `menu`.

A file that fails keeps the last good menu on screen and puts the refusal, named, as a disabled first item in red (and in the log and OSLog). A file that fails at launch, with no last good menu, shows the refusal and the tail alone. Nothing is ever silently dropped.

## Interpolation: the login shell's own

Recommended (Q3): menuz has no interpolation syntax. A string goes to the login shell, which expands it the way the shell expands a double-quoted string: `$VAR`, `${VAR:-default}`, `$(command)`, backticks, `\` escapes, `~` is not expanded inside quotes so `$HOME` is the spelling. Two consequences hv should know:

- A label with no `$` and no backtick is literal and never sent to the shell. A label with one is realised at every menu open (`NSMenuDelegate.menuWillOpen`), all of the menu's such labels and `each` lines in ONE `zsh -ilc` invocation, so a menu with ten dynamic labels costs one shell start, not ten.
- The realisation is asynchronous: the menu opens at once showing the last realised values (the file's text on the first open), and titles update in place when the shell answers; `each` items are inserted and removed in place. Hv sees "fresh a moment later" rather than a menu that hangs on a slow command. The wait is capped at `realise` seconds; a label past the cap keeps its last value and the cap is logged. (The alternative, synchronous realisation in `menuWillOpen`, blocks the menu for the slowest command and is the thing hv would notice.)

`run` lines are never realised by menuz at all: the shell executes them, with the item's parameters exported as variables (below), so `run: arngz apply "$desk"` is ordinary shell and quoting is the shell's. This is what keeps a parameter with a space, a quote or a `;` in it safe: menuz never splices a value into a command line.

## Parameters: one typed form

Ruled (D4, hv: "One form with all params, typed (where possible)"): every parameter of an item is acquired through one form window (a SwiftUI form in an `NSPanel`, Gtools' settings hosting), its fields in the yaml's order, each field typed from the param's `type`; Run and Cancel at the foot:

| `type`   | Field                                                              | Value exported                       |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| `text`   | A text field with `<prompt>` as its label and `<default>` filled in | The text                             |
| `secret` | A secure text field, empty                                         | The text; never written to the log   |
| `choice` | A popup of `choices`, the first selected                           | The chosen line                      |
| `file`   | A path field with a Choose button opening `NSOpenPanel` for a file | The POSIX path                       |
| `folder` | The same, for a folder                                             | The POSIX path                       |

`choices` is a list, or a shell line (`choices: $(ls ~/Desks)`) realised when the dialog opens. Cancel runs nothing and logs `cancelled`. A `required: true` param is refused empty in the form, by name, and Run stays disabled until every refusal is cleared; otherwise an empty answer is an empty variable. The values reach the run as exported variables under the declared names (`$desk`), which is why names are lower-case and refused when the login shell already exports them (validation rule 4).

hv ruled for the form over one dialog per parameter: the dialogs were the standard thing that exists, and the form is what "pops up a window" means once an item has more than one parameter. A `bool` is not a type in v1: a yes-or-no parameter is a `choice` of two lines. A param with no `type` is `text`, which is what the example's `name` param is.

## Running an item

The runner is Gtools' `GtoolsCLI` shape, one shell-out path:

1. `/bin/zsh -ilc "$run"`, so aliases and `PATH` additions from `.zshrc` count, as a terminal would have them (Gtools measured `-ilc` as the invocation that finds what a terminal finds).
2. Environment: launchd's, as the app has it, with `PATH` set to the login shell's capture plus `$MENUZ_HOME/bin` first; `MENUZ_HOME`, `MENUZ_LABEL`, `MENUZ_RUN_ID` and, under `each`, `MENUZ_ITEM`; the item's params by name.
3. Working directory: the item's `cwd`, else the file's, else `$HOME`.
4. stdin is `/dev/null`. A run never has a terminal and never waits for one.
5. Runs are concurrent and independent, each with a run id; nothing is queued and nothing is refused for being busy. A run is detached from the app (D9, hv: "Left running, surely?"): its own session, stdin `/dev/null`, and its stdout and stderr prefixed with the run id and appended to the log by the run's own wrapper shell, not by the app, which also writes the end line with the exit code and the duration. Quit therefore closes nothing a run writes to: runs still in flight are left running, and the log records the quit with the ids still going.

## Output: the log and the notice

Recommended (Q5): hv's simplest option, taken whole. Every run appends to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/menuz/menuz.log`, created on first use:

```
2026-10-16T10:42:03Z run 17 start "Hammerspoon doctor" cwd=~: arngz doctor
[17] hammerspoon  running (pid 4123)
[17] hs tool      /opt/homebrew/bin/hs
[17] ...
2026-10-16T10:42:04Z run 17 exit 0 in 1.3s
```

stdout and stderr lines carry the run id so concurrent runs interleave legibly; the start line prints `cwd` and `run` as written (the run's wrapper expands the cwd, WP-04), which is what keeps a `secret` out of the log (the shell expands `$token`, the log never sees the value). `utilz menuz log` is `tail -f` on that file and prints its path first; **Open Log** in the menu opens it in the default app for `.log`. A log line the app cannot write (the directory unwritable, the disk full) is an error in the app's OSLog and a notification, never a swallowed write.

The notice: a run that exits non-zero posts a macOS notification naming the item and the exit code, so the failure is not silent for a user who is not tailing; `notify: always` posts one on every finish with the last line of output; `notify: never` posts none. The run's wrapper decides whether to post and builds the text, one line, as WP-04 left it, and posts it by running the app's own executable, `"$MENUZ_EXEC" --notify`, with the text exported as `MENUZ_NOTICE` rather than passed as an argument, so no line of a run's output sits in an argv that `ps` would show every local user (`MENUZ_EXEC` is `Bundle.main.executablePath`, exported by the Runner), in place of `osascript` (D13). That arm posts through `UNUserNotificationCenter` under the app's bundle id, so the notice carries menuz's name and icon, and it works whether or not the app is still running: under D9 a run may outlive the app, and a process exec'd from the bundle's executable posts on its own once the bundle id is allowed (measured, D13). The arm waits for the centre's answer: on success it prints `notice posted` and exits 0; when it cannot post it prints why and exits 1, and the wrapper writes that line to the log under the run id, so no notice is dropped silently: `notice not posted: notifications are off for menuz under System Settings > Notifications` when the user turned them off; `notice not posted: menuz is not yet allowed to post notifications: answer macOS's alert, or allow them under System Settings > Notifications > menuz` when the first launch's alert is still up or was withdrawn (the centre's "Notifications are not allowed for this application" with the status not determined, D13); the centre's own words for any other error; `notice not posted: no answer from the notification centre in 10 s` at its deadline. The app requests authorisation at its first launch (`.alert`, `.sound`), so the system's alert comes before any run, and logs the answer; its own notices (a run that could not start, a run id it could not take, the first-launch placement line) go through the same centre, and one about a log it could not write goes to OSLog as well. No file under state, no fallback route, no summary at the next launch. (WP-04 posted from the wrapper through `osascript`, which posts nothing on hv's macOS 27; D13 records the measurement.)

Not in v1, for the rubber-duck to confirm: a console window tailing the log (Gtools' `ConsoleWindowController`, which exists and could be lifted), and output shown in a window per run. hv: "I have a few questions to resolve about what we do with the output." The log is the base either way.

## Watching the file

Conflab's watcher, on two descriptors: the config directory (so an editor's atomic save, which renames a new file into place, and a `git checkout` of the dotfiles both register) and `menuz.yaml` itself. Events are coalesced over 250 ms and then the file is re-read and re-validated; the descriptor on the file is reopened after a rename. A change lands in the menu within a second, measured by hand (AC-03.3). The directory's absence at launch is reported in the menu and the watcher retries every 5 s until `init` creates it.

## The app's command-line arms

`Menuz.app/Contents/MacOS/Menuz --validate [file]`, `--render [file]` and `--version` run without touching the menu bar and exit: `--validate` prints `ok` or every refusal (exit 0 or 2); `--render` prints the menu as the app would show it, labels realised through the shell, indented text, one entry per line (so a test and a human can see what a file becomes). The shim's `validate` and `render` verbs call the installed app's binary, else the Debug build product, else refuse by name. One parser, in the app; the shim parses nothing. `--notify` (WP-06) posts the environment's `MENUZ_NOTICE` as a notification titled `menuz` through `UNUserNotificationCenter` and exits 0 when the centre took it, else prints why and exits 1, and is refused as usage, exit 2, with `MENUZ_NOTICE` unset or empty; the run's wrapper is its caller (Output). `--unregister` (WP-05) unregisters the login item through `SMAppService` and prints the result; the shim's `uninstall` calls it on the installed copy.
